The template seems to involve a bromine attached to aromatic carbon and also a Br-Br? The retro_smarts_template: '[Br;H0;D1;+0:1]-[c;H0;D3;+0:3](:[c:2]):[c:4]>>Br-[Br;H0;D1;+0:1].[c:2]:[cH;D2;+0:3]:[c:4]'

Interpretation: In retrosynthesis, product has Br attached to aromatic carbon (c). The template splits into Br- (bromide) and aromatic hydrogen (c with H). So this seems correct: it breaks C-Br to give Br- and aromatic H.

Thus the mapped_rxn is given: 'Br[Br:5].Br.[CH3:1][C:2]1=[CH:3][CH:4]=[C:6]([CH3:7])[CH:8]=[CH:9]1>>[CH3:1][C:2]1=[CH:3][C:4]([Br:5])=[C:6]([CH3:7])[CH:8]=[CH:9]1'

But this reaction includes a methyl substituent etc. Not generic. However the mapped_rxn is the forward reaction? It seems forward: reactants: Br[Br:5].Br.[CH3...], product: brominated aromatic. That's not exactly our simple benzene case but still the template may apply.
